vulnerability.title: Jenkins exposes encrypted secret values in agent config.xml to Extended Read users

fixed_releases.verified_content: The 2.500 release commit cb753134 has 923cdbc1 as its only parent. In the 2.500 tree Computer.doConfigDotXml (1521-1552) and GetNodeCommand.run both send the serialized agent XML through ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll unless the caller has CONFIGURE, and the @Extension ExtendedReadSecretRedaction replaces encrypted Secret element bodies with ********. The CNA record also lists LTS 2.492.2 as unaffected; that backport was not fetched or asserted.

fix_commits.branch: 2.492.x LTS backport (parent of the 2.492.2 release commit; not fetched locally, ancestry not asserted)

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD publishes a single CVSS 3.1 metric, 4.3 MEDIUM, from the Secondary source (CISA-ADP); there is no Primary metric. OSV/GHSA repeats the same 4.3 vector and records MODERATE. The CNA container has no CVSS metric. Every published severity level is MEDIUM, so the level is consistent and the score is not averaged across sources.

vulnerability.category_l2: Missing redaction on the agent config.xml read paths: users holding Agent/Extended Read but not Agent/Configure receive the XSTREAM XML with encrypted secret values

description: Jenkins exposes an agent's configuration through Computer.doConfigDotXml (REST, GET on .../computer/<name>/config.xml) and the CLI get-node command. Both paths require only Computer.EXTENDED_READ and then serialize the Node with Jenkins.XSTREAM2.toXMLUTF8, which writes every Secret field as its encrypted value. At 2.441 there is no CONFIGURE check on the read path and no redaction: the write path (updateByXml) does require CONFIGURE at line 1578, but the read path at 1551-1560 in Computer.java and line 55 in GetNodeCommand.java returns the XML verbatim. A user granted Agent/Extended Read to inspect agent status can therefore read the encrypted secret values stored in the agent configuration, and those values are intended only for users who may configure the agent. The 2.500 fix 923cdbc1 keeps the EXTENDED_READ requirement and adds a CONFIGURE branch: callers without CONFIGURE get the XML passed through ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll, whose ExtendedReadSecretRedaction extension replaces encrypted Secret bodies with ********. The permission is not enabled by default: Computer.EXTENDED_READ is created with enabled=SystemProperties.getBoolean("hudson.security.ExtendedReadPermission"), so the exposure requires that property to be on.

critical_operation.description: The GET branch of doConfigDotXml checks only EXTENDED_READ (line 1553) and then writes the full node XML with Jenkins.XSTREAM2.toXMLUTF8 at line 1559. Nothing checks CONFIGURE and nothing redacts Secret values, so an Extended Read holder receives the encrypted secret values from the agent configuration.

entry_point.description: Authenticated HTTP GET of /computer/<node>/config.xml (REST) or the CLI get-node command; both require Agent/Extended Read, enabled by hudson.security.ExtendedReadPermission.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA, NVD, OSV and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (agent config.xml read through REST or CLI is not redacted for Extended Read holders) and on the fixed releases (2.500 weekly, 2.492.2 LTS). NVD publishes no Primary metric; the only NVD metric is the CISA-ADP Secondary 4.3 MEDIUM, which OSV/GHSA repeats, and the CNA has no metric, so all published levels are MEDIUM. CWE-312 is recorded by NVD's Secondary source and by GHSA; the CNA lists none. The GHSA ECOSYSTEM range for one package says introduced 2.493, which conflicts with the CNA text (2.499 and earlier) and with the OSV GIT range (introduced 0); this dataset follows the CNA text and the GIT range, and the conflict is recorded rather than silently resolved. This root cause is distinct from the previously promoted jenkins entries: CVE-2024-23897 (CLI arbitrary file read via '@' expansion), CVE-2024-23898 (CLI WebSocket hijacking) and CVE-2024-43045 (missing permission check on the My Views action) involve different entry points and fixes.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Computer.java and GetNodeCommand.java at 2.441 and confirm the GET/CLI read paths require only EXTENDED_READ and emit unredacted XSTREAM2 XML.
An independent reviewer must confirm 923cdbc1 is the fix and is contained in the 2.500 release.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range (weekly <=2.499, LTS <=2.492.1) and that 2.441 is inside it.
An independent reviewer must confirm all published severity levels are MEDIUM (4.3) and record CWE-312.
An independent reviewer must confirm the mechanism is distinct from CVE-2024-23897, CVE-2024-23898 and CVE-2024-43045, and from the sibling CVE-2025-27623 (view config.xml).
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
independent_corrections_accepted: No field was refuted. The reviewer supplied the exact serialization link: XStream2.AssociatedConverterImpl registers Secret$ConverterImpl, whose marshal writes getEncryptedValue() (Secret.java:279), so the exported XML carries the encrypted values rather than plaintext.

The reviewer confirmed the permission caveat independently: Computer.EXTENDED_READ is declared at 1837 with its enable flag at 1843 reading hudson.security.ExtendedReadPermission, which is false by default.

The reviewer explained the GHSA range nuance: the weekly ECOSYSTEM range is encoded as introduced 2.493 -> fixed 2.500, while the LTS range is introduced 0 -> fixed 2.492.2; the union covers 2.441 and the vendor advisory says 2.499 and earlier, so affected_range stays true rather than treating the machine encoding as a contrary fact.
review.duplicate_check: The reviewer confirmed this is distinct from the promoted jenkins entries: CVE-2024-23897 (SECURITY-3314, CLI '@' file read), CVE-2024-23898 (SECURITY-3315, CLI WebSocket origin validation) and CVE-2024-43045 (SECURITY-3349, My Views permission check). It is also distinct from the sibling CVE-2025-27623 (SECURITY-3496), which shares the fix commit but covers view config.xml and View/Read rather than agent config.xml and Agent/Extended Read.

limitations: Static verification only; no Jenkins instance, HTTP request, CLI command or test was executed.

The exposure requires Computer.EXTENDED_READ, which is disabled by default and only enabled when hudson.security.ExtendedReadPermission is set; deployments that never enable it are not exposed through this path.
Only the encrypted value of a Secret is disclosed; decrypting it additionally requires the Jenkins master key. The advisory scores confidentiality as partial (C:L) on that basis.

Only one location row is recorded (Computer.doConfigDotXml). The CLI GetNodeCommand and the sibling View paths (CVE-2025-27623) share the same defect but are not separate locations or vulnerabilities here.
The LTS backport f2eb8ebd and the 2.492.2 branch were not fetched into the local mirror; LTS ancestry is recorded from OSV and the CNA record, not asserted locally.
The GHSA ECOSYSTEM range introduced=2.493 conflicts with the CNA and the OSV GIT range; the conflict is documented, not resolved by choosing one silently.
open_questions: Whether every Node subclass or NodeProperty serializes secrets as Secret (and therefore as encrypted values) was not exhaustively enumerated; the advisory and the regression test use a NodeProperty with a Secret field, which is the documented case.
Whether the 2.492.2 backport is byte-identical in behaviour was not checked locally.
